Q: altair mark_area not working with alt.Y2Value or alt.value A: 
import altair as alt
import polars as pl
import numpy as np

data = pl.DataFrame({
    "x": np.arange(1, 4),
    "y": np.arange(1, 4),
})

base = alt.Chart(data).encode(alt.X("x"))

line = base.mark_line().encode(alt.Y("y"))

area_above = base.mark_area(color="black", opacity=0.2).encode(
    alt.Y("y"),
    # Set the baseline to a value higher than your data max
    # You can use a high number or the 'max' of your column
    alt.Y2(datum=data["y"].max()) 
)

line + area_above

Q: PowerShell Strings from headers is this possible? A:

You can use Set-Variable and Get-Variable when you want to refer to a variable by its stringed name.

$ImportedCsv = @'
Value1,Value2,Value3,Value4
10,20,30,40
11,12,13,14
'@ | ConvertFrom-Csv -Delimiter ','

# This way you have $HeaderArray, which contains all the names of the variables
# you just created, for later use.  
$HeaderArray = foreach ($HeaderName in $ImportedCsv[0].PSObject.Properties.name) {
    Set-Variable -Name $HeaderName -Value ($ImportedCsv.$HeaderName -join ',') 
    $HeaderName
}
$HeaderArray

foreach ($Header in $HeaderArray) {
    '${0}: {1}' -f $Header, (Get-Variable -Name $Header -ValueOnly)
}

--

# Extra:   
# By using the switch -PassThru, $HeaderArray instead contains a linked list of the generated variables.   
# Changes to the variables after the creation also reflect in the array
$HeaderArray = foreach ($HeaderName in $ImportedCsv[0].PSObject.Properties.name) {
    Set-Variable -Name $HeaderName -Value ($ImportedCsv.$HeaderName -join ',') -PassThru
}
$HeaderArray

Set-Variable $HeaderArray[0].Name -Value 'Omega'

foreach ($Header in $HeaderArray) {
    '${0}: {1}; Also: {2}' -f $Header.Name, $header.value, (Get-Variable -Name $header.name -ValueOnly)
}
